modules.title: Introduction
modules.description: Introduction to Data Science, including its definition, required skills, tools, data types, data collections, preprocessing, data analysis, and major types of analytics.
modules.overview: This module introduces the foundations of Data Science. It covers what Data Science is, the skills and tools needed for data science work, different data types and collections, data preprocessing, and the major approaches used for analysing data.
objectives: Understand the definition and fundamentals of Data Science.
Identify the skills and tools required for Data Science.
Understand different data types and data collections.
Explain data preprocessing and data analysis.
Differentiate descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive, exploratory, and mechanistic analysis.

modules.title: Data Extraction
modules.description: Extracting meaning from data through feature selection, user retention, filters, wrappers, entropy, decision tree algorithms, random forests, the dimensionality problem, SVD, and PCA.
modules.overview: This module focuses on extracting useful information from data and selecting informative features. It introduces feature-selection approaches, decision trees, random forests, dimensionality problems, singular value decomposition, and principal component analysis.
objectives: Understand how useful meaning can be extracted from data.
Explain feature selection and feature-selection methods.
Understand entropy and decision tree algorithms.
Describe random forests and their use in data analysis.
Understand the dimensionality problem, SVD, and PCA.

modules.title: Data Visualization
modules.description: Visualizing data using Matplotlib, Pandas, Seaborn, line plots, bar plots, histograms, density plots, scatter plots, facet grids, and categorical data visualizations.
modules.overview: This module introduces Python-based data visualization. It covers the Matplotlib API, plotting with Pandas and Seaborn, and a range of plots for understanding distributions, relationships, and categorical data.
objectives: Understand the basic Matplotlib API.
Create visualizations using Pandas and Seaborn.
Represent data using line plots, bar plots, histograms, and density plots.
Create scatter plots and facet grids.
Visualize categorical data effectively.

modules.title: Statistical Thinking
modules.description: Understanding distributions through histograms, outliers, variance, probability mass functions, cumulative distribution functions, percentile-based statistics, random numbers, and probability distributions.
modules.overview: This module develops statistical thinking for understanding and representing data distributions. It covers histograms, outliers, variance, PMFs, CDFs, percentile-based statistics, random numbers, and important probability distributions including exponential, normal, and lognormal distributions.
objectives: Represent and plot distributions using histograms.
Identify outliers and summarize distributions.
Understand variance and probability mass functions.
Represent and interpret cumulative distribution functions and percentile-based statistics.
Understand exponential, normal, and lognormal distributions.

modules.title: Time Series Analysis and Predictive Modeling
modules.description: Analysing time series through importing and cleaning data, plotting, moving averages, missing values, serial correlation, autocorrelation, predictive modeling, model evaluation, model-solution building, and sentiment analysis.
modules.overview: This module introduces time series analysis and predictive modeling. It covers importing and cleaning time-series data, plotting and moving averages, handling missing values, serial correlation and autocorrelation, predictive modeling, evaluation of predictive models, building predictive model solutions, and sentiment analysis.
objectives: Import, clean, and plot time-series data.
Understand moving averages and missing values in time series.
Explain serial correlation and autocorrelation.
Understand predictive modeling and evaluate predictive models.
Build predictive model solutions and understand sentiment analysis.

experiments.name: Working with Different Data Formats using Pandas
experiments.description: A practical exploration of CSV, JSON, and Excel data handling with Pandas, including reading, writing, parsing, and working with multiple sheets.

subExperiments.name: CSV File Handling
subExperiments.description: Read an online CSV dataset, write CSV output, and work with tab-delimited student data.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

# 1A.1 - Read an online CSV file
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/iris.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(url)
print("First five rows of the dataset:")
print(df.head())
print("\nDataset Information:")
print(df.info())
print("\nNumber of rows and columns:")
print(df.shape)

# 1A.2 - Write the DataFrame to CSV
output_file = "iris_output.csv"
df.to_csv(output_file, index=False)
print(f"\nThe dataset has been successfully written to {output_file}")

# 1A.3 - Create a tab-delimited student file, then read it
student_data = {
    "Roll_No": [101, 102, 103, 104],
    "Name": ["Anusha", "Babitha", "Charitha", "Deepika"],
    "Department": ["IT", "IT", "CSE", "ECE"],
    "Percentage": [89, 92, 88, 85]
}
student_df = pd.DataFrame(student_data)
student_df.to_csv("students.txt", sep="\t", index=False)
print("\nData successfully written to students.txt")

print("\nStudent data read from the tab-delimited file:")
print(pd.read_csv("students.txt", sep="\t"))

subExperiments.name: JSON File Handling
subExperiments.description: Create JSON records, read JSON files, parse JSON text, and consume JSON data from an API.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO

# 1B.1 - Write a DataFrame to JSON
student_data = {
    "Roll No": [101, 102, 103, 104],
    "Name": ["Anu", "Bobby", "Cheriy", "Duke"],
    "Department": ["IT", "IT", "CSE", "DS"]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(student_data)
df.to_json("students.json", orient="records", indent=4)
print("JSON file created successfully")

# 1B.2 - Read the JSON file
print("\nStudent Data")
print(pd.read_json("students.json"))

# 1B.3 - Parse JSON text directly
json_data = """
[
    {"RollNo": 101, "Name": "Anu", "Marks": 89},
    {"RollNo": 102, "Name": "Bobby", "Marks": 92},
    {"RollNo": 103, "Name": "Charitha", "Marks": 88}
]
"""
parsed_df = pd.read_json(StringIO(json_data))
print("\nParsed JSON Data")

# 1B.4 - Read JSON data from a public API

api_df = pd.read_json(url)

subExperiments.name: Excel File Handling
subExperiments.description: Write and read Excel files, create multiple worksheets, and load all sheets with Pandas.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

# 1C.1 - Write a student DataFrame to Excel
student_data = {
    "Roll No": [101, 102, 103, 104],
    "Name": ["Anu", "Bobby", "Cherry", "Duke"],
    "Department": ["IT", "IT", "CSE", "DS"],
    "Percentage": [89, 92, 88, 85]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(student_data)
df.to_excel("students.xlsx", sheet_name="Student-Details", index=False)
print("Data successfully written to students.xlsx")

# 1C.2 - Read the Excel file
read_df = pd.read_excel("students.xlsx", sheet_name="Student-Details")
print("\nData read from Excel File:")
print(read_df)

# 1C.3 - Write multiple DataFrames to different sheets
course_data = {
    "Course-ID": ["C101", "C102", "C103"],
    "Course-Name": ["Python", "DataScience", "Machine Learning"],
    "Credits": [4, 3, 4]
}
courses_df = pd.DataFrame(course_data)
with pd.ExcelWriter("college-data.xlsx", engine="openpyxl") as writer:
    df.iloc[:3].to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Students", index=False)
    courses_df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Courses", index=False)
print("\nMultiple sheets successfully written to college-data.xlsx")

# 1C.4 - Read all sheets
excel_data = pd.read_excel("college-data.xlsx", sheet_name=None)
print("\nAvailable Sheets:")
print(list(excel_data.keys()))
print("\nStudent Sheet:")
print(excel_data["Students"])
print("\nCourse Sheet:")
print(excel_data["Courses"])

subExperiments.name: SQLite Database Operations
subExperiments.description: Create a SQLite table, insert records, query them with Pandas, then update and delete a record.
subExperiments.code:
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

conn = sqlite3.connect("students.db")
cursor = conn.cursor()

cursor.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS students
                  (id INTEGER, name TEXT)""")
cursor.execute("INSERT INTO students VALUES (1, 'John')")
conn.commit()

df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM students", conn)
print(df)

cursor.execute("UPDATE students SET name = 'Alice' WHERE id = 1")
cursor.execute("DELETE FROM students WHERE id = 1")
conn.commit()
conn.close()

subExperiments.name: Missing Values and Duplicates
subExperiments.description: Inspect missing-value masks, remove incomplete rows, fill missing values, and remove duplicate records.
subExperiments.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

data = {"A": [1, 2, np.nan], "B": [4, np.nan, np.nan]}

df_filled = df.fillna(0)
print("\nRows after dropna():")
print(df_clean)
print("\nValues after fillna(0):")

df = df.drop_duplicates()

subExperiments.name: Convert Periods and Periodlndex objects to another frequency
subExperiments.description: The asfreq() method in Pandas converts Period and PeriodIndex objects from one frequency to another, such as converting monthly periods into daily or yearly periods. It helps analyze time-series data at different time intervals. The freq parameter specifies the target frequency, and the how parameter ('start' or 'end') determines whether to select the beginning or end of the original period when converting to a lower frequency.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

# 1. Create a monthly Period
p = pd.Period("2026-01", freq="M")
print("Original monthly period:")
print(p)

# 2. Convert monthly Period to daily frequency
print("\nMonthly to daily (start):")
print(p.asfreq("D", how="start"))
print("\nMonthly to daily (end):")
print(p.asfreq("D", how="end"))

# 3. Create a PeriodIndex
period_index = pd.period_range(start="2026-01", periods=3, freq="M")
print("\nOriginal PeriodIndex:")
print(period_index)

# 4. Convert PeriodIndex to daily frequency
print("\nPeriodIndex to daily (start):")
print(period_index.asfreq("D", how="start"))
print("\nPeriodIndex to daily (end):")
print(period_index.asfreq("D", how="end"))

subExperiments.name: Convert Series and DataFrame objects indexed by timestamps to periods
subExperiments.description: The `to_period()` method in Pandas converts a Series or DataFrame index containing timestamps into a PeriodIndex, representing a specific time period such as a day, month, quarter, or year. It is useful for time-series analysis when data needs to be grouped or analyzed by periods rather than individual timestamps. The `freq` parameter specifies the required frequency, such as `'M'` for monthly or `'Y'` for yearly periods.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

# 1. Create a Series with timestamp index
dates = pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-10", "2026-02-15", "2026-03-20", "2026-04-25"])
sales = pd.Series([1000, 1500, 1800, 2200], index=dates)
print("Original Series:")
print(sales)

# 2. Convert Series from timestamps to monthly periods
print("\nSeries converted to monthly periods:")
print(sales.to_period("M"))

# 3. Create a DataFrame with timestamp index
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {"Sales": [1000, 1500, 1800, 2200], "Profit": [200, 300, 400, 500]},
    index=dates
)
print("\nOriginal DataFrame:")
print(df)

# 4. Convert DataFrame to monthly periods
print("\nDataFrame converted to monthly periods:")
print(df.to_period("M"))

subExperiments.name: Resampling, Downsampling, and Upsampling
subExperiments.description: Resample hourly data, aggregate larger intervals, and upsample to 30-minute intervals with optional forward filling.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

dates = pd.date_range("2026-01-01 00:00", periods=12, freq="h")
values = [10, 12, 15, 14, 18, 20, 22, 21, 25, 28, 30, 32]
ts = pd.Series(values, index=dates)
print("Original hourly time series:")
print(ts)

print("\nResampling - 3-hour mean:")
print(ts.resample("3h").mean())

print("\nDownsampling - 4-hour sum:")
print(ts.resample("4h").sum())

print("\nUpsampling - 30-minute intervals:")
print(ts.resample("30min").asfreq())

print("\nUpsampling with forward fill:")
print(ts.resample("30min").ffill())

experiments.name: Data Aggregation
experiments.description: Group tabular data using single or multiple keys, calculate grouped summary statistics, and perform exploratory data analysis on an online dataset.

subExperiments.name: Group Data Using Single and Multiple Keys
subExperiments.description: Create a DataFrame, group records by one or multiple keys, select groups, and calculate average marks.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "Name": ["Ravi", "Sita", "Arun", "Priya", "Kiran", "Anil", "Lakshmi", "Rahul"],
    "Department": ["CSE", "CSE", "ECE", "ECE", "CSE", "ECE", "CSE", "ECE"],
    "Year": [2, 2, 3, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2],
    "Marks": [85, 90, 78, 88, 75, 82, 95, 70]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print("Original DataFrame:")
print(df)

print("\nGroup by Department:")
for department, group in df.groupby("Department"):
    print(f"\nDepartment: {department}")
    print(group)
print("\nAverage marks by Department:")
print(df.groupby("Department")["Marks"].mean())

print("\nGroup by Department and Year:")
for key, group in df.groupby(["Department", "Year"]):
    print(f"\nGroup: {key}")
    print(group)
print("\nAverage marks by Department and Year:")
print(df.groupby(["Department", "Year"])["Marks"].mean())

subExperiments.name: Compute Summary Statistics Using Aggregation
subExperiments.description: Calculate sum, mean, and standard deviation for Marks and Attendance grouped by department.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "Department": ["CSE", "CSE", "CSE", "ECE", "ECE", "ECE", "EEE", "EEE", "EEE"],
    "Marks": [80, 75, 85, 70, 65, 75, 90, 85, 95],
    "Attendance": [90, 85, 95, 80, 75, 85, 95, 90, 100]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
print("Original DataFrame:")
print(df)

summary = df.groupby("Department").aggregate({
    "Marks": ["sum", "mean", "std"],
    "Attendance": ["sum", "mean", "std"]
})
print("\nSummary statistics:")
print(summary)

subExperiments.name: GroupBy and Exploratory Data Analysis on an Online Dataset
subExperiments.description: Load the online Iris dataset, inspect and summarize it, group by one or multiple columns, and calculate species-level statistics.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

# Read the online Iris dataset
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/iris.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(url)

print("First 5 records:")
print(df.head())
print("\nDataset information:")
df.info()
print("\nStatistical summary:")
print(df.describe())

print("\nGroupBy using a single column:")
print(df.groupby("species")["sepal_length"].agg(
    ["count", "sum", "mean", "std", "min", "max"]
))

print("\nGroupBy using multiple columns:")
print(df.groupby(["species", "sepal_width"])["sepal_length"].mean().head(15))

print("\nSummary statistics by species:")
print(df.groupby("species").agg({
    "sepal_length": ["mean", "std", "min", "max"],
    "sepal_width": ["mean", "std", "min", "max"],
    "petal_length": ["mean", "std", "min", "max"],
    "petal_width": ["mean", "std", "min", "max"]
}))

print("\nNumber of records in each species:")
print(df["species"].value_counts())
print("\nAverage petal length by species:")
print(df.groupby("species")["petal_length"].mean())
print("\nAverage petal width by species:")
print(df.groupby("species")["petal_width"].mean())
print("\nMaximum sepal length by species:")
print(df.groupby("species")["sepal_length"].max())

projects.title: Stock Day Tracker
projects.tagline: NSE/BSE Market Intelligence & Day-by-Day Price Movement Analytics
projects.description: Developed a stock market tracking web application that displays day-by-day price movements of NSE/BSE stocks through interactive weekly and monthly views. Implemented watchlists, stock search, price change and percentage tracking, heatmap visualization, and stock detail charts. Designed a modular market data architecture supporting simulated data and external market data providers, with caching to improve efficiency.
keyFeatures: Interactive weekly and monthly views displaying day-by-day price movements of NSE/BSE stocks.
Customizable watchlists with instant stock search and real-time ticker tracking.
High-contrast price change metrics with green/red percentage tracking and volume signals.
Dynamic sector heatmap visualization for rapid cross-market sector performance analysis.
Detailed stock breakdown charts with moving averages, OHLCV data, and time-frame zoom.
Modular market data architecture with automated fallback between live external APIs and simulated feeds.
Multi-level in-memory data caching layer with TTL expiration for high throughput and reduced latency.
projects.architecture: Vite + React.js frontend interface with modular data hooks, coupled with an Express.js backend caching proxy layer communicating with external Market Data APIs and in-memory cache stores.

projects.title: Civic Issue Reporting Platform (CivicConnect)
projects.tagline: Full-Stack Civic Grievance Management, Role-Based Redressal & Resolution Analytics
projects.description: Developed a full-stack civic grievance management platform that enables citizens to report public issues and track their resolution status. Implemented role-based access for citizens, government officials, and administrators, including complaint assignment, status updates, activity timelines, and feedback submission. Integrated JWT-based authentication, password hashing, and an SQLite database to manage users, complaints, and administrative analytics.
keyFeatures: Citizen public grievance submission with geo-tagging, categorisation, and multimedia uploads.
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) securely separating Citizens, Government Officials, and System Administrators.
Dynamic complaint assignment engine routing issues to relevant department officers based on jurisdiction.
Live status progression (Submitted → Under Review → Assigned → In Progress → Resolved → Closed).
Interactive activity timeline displaying transparent chronological audit trails of official actions.
Citizen feedback and star-rating mechanism upon issue resolution for accountability.
Stateless JWT-based authentication paired with Bcrypt salted cryptographic password hashing.
Normalized SQLite relational schema managing users, grievances, department allocations, and audit logs.
Administrative analytics dashboard with SLA turnaround tracking and department resolution charts.
projects.architecture: Full-stack client-server platform powered by Node.js and Express.js REST endpoints, SQLite relational database layer with foreign key cascades, and stateless JWT token authentication middleware.
